versions.line: When the chat starts a task or passes your message on, it now says so in one line, after it has done it
The Finished tab and its list are now called Done, the same word a card says, so the tabs read All
Every reply about a task in the chat has the colour of that task's card as it stands now
Every task card now says how full its task is, on any model and whether it is at work, waiting or finished
A result in the chat turns green once you mark its task as done, as its card does in the panel
When a connector such as Higgsfield is missing or needs signing in
A go-ahead you type in the chat while a change waits is read for what you mean, in whatever words
Refresh, beside Open panel and Close panel above the chat, puts the panel back as it first opens
Finished shows one page of 40 tasks at a time, with Newer and Older under it
The north star on Progress is now the bigger vision your work serves, in at most ten words
A task's result reaches the chat as a few short lines
The task panel has a row of tabs under its header
The north star on top of Progress is picked each month from all you did that month
The Stats timeline now shows every helper as a bar of its own, in its own model's colour, beside the tasks
The Progress chart no longer shows fewer squares as the panel gets wider
Code copies whose work is merged are now removed even when they hold only what a build makes (a type cache
A pressed button in the panel or the bar keeps spinning until the panel shows what the press did
Every question on a task's card now has Skip this one
With tasks at work the panel and the bar are asked for far less often
A panel drawn again with nothing new in it costs less in a chat with many tasks
A pointer resting on the disk's speed in the line above the prompt shows how much disk space is used
With several tasks and helpers at work, Claudopus uses less of the processor
Every value on a question or a result that you would paste somewhere else, such as an account or case number
Claudopus installs and runs on Windows, in the Claude app's Code tab or in a terminal
A busy chat uses far less of the processor
A task that can no longer be reached, such as one a rewind of the chat left behind
On battery, Claude's commands get only a few fast cores at once, and the rest move to the Mac's slow
A task's part of its result, passed on by the chat, shows in that task's coloured box
When your Mac is busy, Claudopus no longer reloads itself again and again in a chat whose Claudopus is…
The grey quote over a coloured reply is now the message it answers wherever you sent it
